subject: Request: provisional capacity uplift and phased invoicing for pilot
messages:
From: Kirti Rao <kirti@nimhealth.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-09T08:12:00Z
Subject: Request: provisional capacity uplift and phased invoicing for pilot

Hi Mateo,

We're running into higher-than-expected traffic during our week-3 pilot window. Yesterday we spiked ~3.5x above our forecasted token usage and hit the current quota cap mid-day, which throttled a subset of our ingestion pipelines. We have a hard customer deadline next Friday and need a short-term uplift to avoid lost telemetry.

Can Redwood provisionally increase our throughput ceiling by ~2x for 72 hours while we stabilize? Ideally we'd: 
- Get the uplift within the next 48 hours
- Have billing for the uplift phased so we don't get a single large overrun invoice (we can accept a provisional charge + final true-up)

I'm attaching a small usage snapshot from the last 7 days to show the spike. Open to a one-off credit in return for committing to a 12-month minimum if that helps.

Thanks,
Kirti
Director of Integrations
Nimbus Health

Attachment: usage_snapshot_q2.csv (CSV, 38KB)
From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Kirti Rao <kirti@nimhealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-09T10:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Request: provisional capacity uplift and phased invoicing for pilot

Kirti — thanks for the heads up and the CSV. Sorry to hear the pilot hit that spike. We can move quickly here.

Two parts: capacity and billing.
- Capacity: I can request an emergency temporary QPS/headroom bump for 72 hours. That will need approval from sales ops to allocate short-term capacity.
- Billing: we can offer a phased approach: an upfront provisional fee to cover immediate extra capacity and then a final true-up against actual usage at the end of the month. We can also apply a small one-time credit if you convert to a 12-month commitment.

Looping in Ben to propose the provisional uplift and the provisional-rate sheet. Ben — can you propose the uplift parameters (rate, credit, DocuSign for a short amendment) so we can get Nimbus back online within 48 hours?

Mateo
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

On 2027-05-09 08:12, Kirti Rao wrote:
> Hi Mateo,
>
> We're running into higher-than-expected traffic during our week-3 pilot window...

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Kirti Rao <kirti@nimhealth.com>
Date: 2027-05-09T14:22:00Z
Subject: Re: Request: provisional capacity uplift and phased invoicing for pilot

Hey all — quick proposal so we can move.

Proposal (short-term emergency uplift):
- Uplift: 2x token throughput ceiling for 72 hours starting on approval
- Provisional charge: 30% of the estimated overage (billed as a provisional invoice immediately)
- Final true-up: reconcile actual usage at month-end; provisional charge applied against final amount
- One-time credit: 15% credit on the provisional charge if Nimbus signs a 12-month commit within 10 business days

I've attached a one-page provisional-rate-sheet with the numbers and the DocuSign amendment template for a short-term uplift addendum. If this looks reasonable I can start the DocuSign and notify ops to allocate the capacity.

Questions I expect from procurement: where the uplift is applied on the invoice, and whether the provisional charge is refundable if actual usage is lower than estimated. Our standard is to reconcile and refund any over-collection in the final true-up.

Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachment: provisional-rate-sheet.pdf (PDF, 18KB)
From: Kirti Rao <kirti@nimhealth.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@nimhealth.com
Date: 2027-05-10T09:11:00Z
Subject: Re: Request: provisional capacity uplift and phased invoicing for pilot

Ben — thanks for the fast turnaround. A few follow-ups from procurement and legal: 
1) Procurement asks that the provisional charge be explicitly refundable if final usage is below the provisional estimate (we prefer net-refund, not just application against future invoices).
2) Legal wants the DocuSign amendment to be limited to the 72-hour uplift window with no standing rate changes.
3) We are willing to sign a 12-month commit if Redwood can: (a) lock the uplift premium (i.e., the uplift's unit rate) for the first 6 months of the commit and (b) increase the credit to 20% on the provisional charge.

Can Redwood confirm these three items? If yes, we can send a PO and ask legal to fast-track signatures. We need the capacity uplift before Friday (2027-05-14) to complete the pilot validation.

—Kirti
From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Kirti Rao <kirti@nimhealth.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-11T16:03:00Z
Subject: Re: Request: provisional capacity uplift and phased invoicing for pilot

Kirti — quick confirmation and next steps: 

1) Refundable provisional charge: Sales is OK to make the provisional charge refundable if final true-up shows lower usage. We will issue a net refund against the invoice.
2) DocuSign scope: We'll limit the amendment to the 72-hour uplift window with a clear clause that no baseline price changes unless mutually agreed.
3) Commit incentive: We can move the credit to 20% on the provisional charge and hold the uplift premium steady for the first 6 months of any signed 12-month commitment (legal to finalize language).

Ben — please prepare the DocuSign with the updated language (refund clause and commit incentive) and mark the uplift start date as pending upon signature/PO. Ops: please standby to allocate the 72-hour uplift once DocuSign is accepted.

Kirti — once we have the signed amendment and PO I will confirm the uplift window and share the temporary routing map for the requests.

Thanks,
Mateo
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
